_comment: Vectors for the whole-bill / per-line ROUND OFF rule and the four-decimal
voucher RATE, run against BOTH implementations by scripts/check-mirrors.js
The table lives in THIS repo rather than in either submodule for the reason
the voucher-lifecycle table does: two copies of a vector file in two
independent git repos is the same mirror problem one level up.
Each row carries its own `want`, so a rule both sides forgot TOGETHER is
caught too — a two-way parity check passes that, which is why every
*-rules.ts module in qa-artifacts is a restatement rather than an import.

adjustment.why: no mode, no adjustment — the one that must never move a total
rounds DOWN — the ordinary case, and why the charge amount is signed
an empty voucher rounds to nothing

a sub-paisa base. ⚠️ This row does NOT discriminate the paise-first rounding — float truncation puts both orderings on 0 — which is why the two below it exist; it is kept because it pins the answer at a base that LOOKS like it should move

⚠️ the base is rounded to PAISE FIRST, so 0.4996 is 0.50 and JS rounds that half UP to 1. Drop the round2 and the base rounds DOWN to 0 instead, flipping the adjustment to −0.5 — this row is what catches that ordering being lost on BOTH sides at once
the same ordering at a five-rupee step, where the sign flip is a whole 5 apart
exactly half a step — both sides must break the tie the same way

step.why: an unrecognised mode rounds to nothing rather than throwing

lineAmount.why: the .5 tie, which JS rounds toward +∞

rateFromAmount.why: back-solving the operator's own line — note the rate is NOT the round figure it looks like it should be, which is exactly why two decimals could not express it
a rate that needs all four decimals
no quantity to divide by — 0, never Infinity, which would reach the DTO as a number and be stored
